description: THE HIGHEST-PRIORITY GAP IN THE ENGINE. Today `.chief/verify.sh` is a pass/fail test oracle: it answers 'did the gates exit 0', nothing more. That is exactly the reward shape the RLVR critique indicts — 'there is no penalty for eroding codebase maintainability', because tests return in seconds while shotgun surgery shows up in weeks. Chief therefore maximizes 'how much can we queue for the agent' while gating on a signal that is blind to the damage the research documents (Faros AI: +242.7% incidents per PR, +31.3% of PRs skipping review; SlopCodeBench: cyclomatic complexity grew across checkpoints for EVERY model tested, and 89-98% of lines tripped slop rules regardless of model). This tasklist gives the merge gate a second, DETERMINISTIC axis: measure code-quality metrics on the branch, compare them against the base, and BLOCK a merge that makes the codebase materially worse — even when every test is green. Modeled on talos's proven 'ratchet' (a monotone baseline that may improve and may not regress) and on SlopCodeBench's 41 deterministic measures (NO model judgment anywhere in the gate — a model scoring a model's work reintroduces the same blind spot). Scope: a metrics tool shipped with the engine, its wiring into `.chief/verify.sh` + `templates/verify.sh`, a per-repo config with a baseline file, and docs. See ../AGENTIC-ENGINEERING-ADVISORY.md §3 and §6.1.

userStories.title: A deterministic code-quality metrics tool
userStories.description: Ship a tool that computes objective, reproducible metrics over a set of changed files. Deterministic only — no LLM, no network, no judgment calls.
acceptanceCriteria: A metrics command (shipped with the engine, e.g. `engine/quality.sh` or a `chief quality` subcommand) computes, for a given file set, a documented metric record: total/added/removed source lines, file count, function count, mean and max function length, max nesting depth, duplicated-block count and percentage, single-use function count, and per-file lint-violation counts where a linter is configured — matching SlopCodeBench's deterministic families (size, complexity, duplication, decomposition, rule violations)

Metrics are LANGUAGE-AWARE BUT DEGRADE HONESTLY: a language-agnostic core (lines, files, duplication by normalized-line hashing, nesting via brace/indent heuristics) always runs; richer per-language analyzers run only when the toolchain is present, and a language with no analyzer is REPORTED AS UNMEASURED — never scored as 0 and never silently skipped (the same `not_measured` discipline talos uses; a metric that vanishes is worse than one that is absent)
Output is a stable, sorted JSON record suitable for committing as a baseline: identical inputs produce byte-identical output, with no timestamps, no absolute paths, and no host-specific values
The tool runs offline with no network and adds no new hard runtime dependency beyond what the engine already requires (`jq`); anything richer is opt-in and its absence degrades to UNMEASURED

userStories.title: Ratchet semantics: block a merge that makes the codebase materially worse
userStories.description: Compare the branch's metrics against the base and block on regression beyond a configured tolerance. Never absolute thresholds — a legacy repo must not be unmergeable on day one.
acceptanceCriteria: The gate computes metrics for the SAME changed-file scope on the branch and on `$CHIEF_BASE_BRANCH`, and evaluates DELTAS — a repo with pre-existing high complexity is not blocked for its history, only for what this branch adds (mirrors the existing path-scoped, diff-driven design of `.chief/verify.sh`)

A committed baseline file (e.g. `.chief/quality-baseline.json`) records the accepted metric record; the gate BLOCKS when a tracked metric regresses beyond its configured tolerance and ALLOWS when metrics hold or improve — a monotone ratchet, with `--write-baseline` as the explicit, reviewable re-baseline escape hatch

Thresholds and the tracked-metric set are configured per repo (in `.chief/config` or a sibling), with documented defaults; a repo may disable individual metrics but the DISABLING IS VISIBLE in the config diff, never implicit

Blocking output names the offending metric, its base value, its branch value, the tolerance, and the files that contributed most — an operator must be able to act on the message without rerunning anything
The gate is skippable exactly like the existing suite (`CHIEF_VERIFY_TESTS=0`-style env, documented) so iterating locally is not punished, and `NO_VERIFY=1` continues to bypass the whole hook

userStories.title: Wire it into the hook, the template, and the docs
userStories.description: Make it the default for chief itself and for every repo scaffolded by `chief init`, and document the contract.
acceptanceCriteria: `.chief/verify.sh` (this repo, self-hosting) runs the quality ratchet as a gate, path-scoped and cheapest-first consistent with the existing structure, and blocks on regression
`templates/verify.sh` gains the same gate (commented, and off or lenient by default so `chief init` in a brownfield repo is not immediately unmergeable) plus a baseline-bootstrap instruction

`docs/verify-hook.md` documents the quality axis: what is measured, ratchet semantics, the baseline file, re-baselining, per-repo config, and the explicit statement that the gate is deterministic and contains no model judgment

A hermetic test asserts the ratchet: a branch that adds a deeply-nested duplicated block regresses a tracked metric and is BLOCKED; a branch that refactors it away IMPROVES the metric and is ALLOWED; a language with no analyzer reports UNMEASURED rather than passing silently
